newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late rubber stable, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late rubber stable, trade quiet.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices were stable in late trading on Monday on thin buying interest, traders said.
They said there were no signs of market intervention by the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO), adding that they were sceptical the grouping would act at current levels.
"It looks like INRO is waiting for prices to go down further," one trader said. "I, personally, am not very optimistic that INRO will intervene at current levels."

INRO's five-day moving price indicator dipped below its "may-buy" level of 183.00 Malaysian/Singapore cents last Friday, but the grouping has kept the markets guessing over when it would start buying to prop up prices.
The traders also said SIR20 remained under pressure because of cheaper Thai rubber prices.
"This is an abnormal situation because Thailand's RSS3 prices are at a discount to Indonesia's SIR20," one said. "RSS3 is a form of pure rubber and usually fetches a higher price."
The traders said August/September shipment SIR20 offer prices were up 0.25-0.50 cents at 43.50-44.00 cents/lb fob Medan, 43.25-43.75 cents fob Palembang and 43.00-43.25 fob Padang and Surbaya.
